beats.text: You remember their face. Their job. Their dog. But not their name.
In one experiment, people saw a face and were told: this man is a baker. Others were told: his name is Baker.
Same word. But the job was remembered far better than the name.
It's called the Baker baker paradox.
A baker comes with bread, flour and ovens. A name like Baker comes with nothing.
So give names a hook. Picture Mister Baker holding a loaf of bread.

sources: McWeeny, Young, Hay & Ellis (1987). Putting names to faces. British Journal of Psychology 78. Same word remembered better as an occupation than as a surname.
Cohen (1990). Why is it difficult to put names to faces? British Journal of Psychology 81. Via ScienceABC.
